name: Mt Flagstone
description:
Mingela Range, Mingela Stage Forest
Leader: Luen Warneke
For more information, contact 	info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com

Saturday, 27th May, 2023
Mt Flagstone, Mingela State Park
 
Who is leading: Luen Warneke

Difficulty: Grade 4

Distance: ~5km circuit
 
Description:
This walk is accessed via private property .

Our adventure will take us through the stunning Mingela State Forest, covering an area of 7,800 hectares and featuring four named mountains. We will trek towards our primary goal, Mount Flagstone, standing tall at 591 meters. 
Along the way, you'll be treated to picturesque views of Bowling Green Bay National Park, Pinnacles National Park, Ross River Dam, and Mount Stuart Range. Capture these breathtaking vistas with your camera as we navigate the open grasslands and ridgelines.

As we explore this untamed landscape, we will also pass by seasonal creeks, which may flow after heavy rains. Please note that there are no marked tracks within Mingela State Forest, so we will rely on our experienced guides to lead the way.

Tips:
The best time to hike this area is during the cooler months, as summer can be extremely hot and humid.
Access to Mingela State Forest may be limited due to surrounding private properties. Our guides will ensure we traverse authorized routes only.

During our bushwalk, we will be traversing uneven ground and terrain, which include steep inclines, declines, and loose surfaces. To minimise the risk of falls and injuries, please wear appropriate footwear with good traction, such as hiking boots or trail shoes. 

Additionally, our experienced guides will provide instructions on how to navigate challenging areas safely.

Don't miss this unique opportunity to explore the beautiful Mingela State Forest and conquer Mount Flagstone with fellow bushwalking enthusiasts! Secure your spot today and prepare for an unforgettable adventure.
 
 
Duration: Full day : 7:00 am to about 5:00 pm. 
 
Meeting Time:
7:00 am - Meeting location will be emailed closer to the time 
 
What do you need:
Wear appropriate footwear, i.e., enclosed sturdy shoes that grip on rocks.
Gaiters are necessary as we will be traversing long grass
Appropriate clothing - long covered pants and shirts/ tops for sun protection and protection against scratches.
Gloves.
Drinking water - carry 3-5 litres of water as there are NO REFILL POINTS on trail.  
The club also recommends use of electrolytes during the day.
Bring food and snacks to suit your energy needs for a full day hike
Bushwalkers should bring their own personal (minimal) first aid kit, headtorch, and whistle, etc.
Luen will also have his personal minimal first aid kit and PLB. The club does not provide a group first aid kit.

----------

Register - Mt Flagstone
Must be over 18 yrs to participate.   

If conditions on the day are unsuitable then the route and walk length may be changed at the leader’s discretion. 
 
Please Note - If you are a new walker/non-member who has not walked with us before – please contact the walk leader before RSVPing. 


Fee: non-members/visitors/-  $5 . TBWC Club members - Free. 
You can become a TBWC member after 3 walks as a visitor



To register for the walk, Please use the form below. 

For Club Members – if the RSVP registration is fully subscribed, contact the leader direct to discuss participation.

name: Killymoon Creek Bowling Green Bay National Park
description:
Sunday, 14th May, 2023 
Killymoon Creek
Bowling Green Bay National Park

Leader: Molly 

Rated: Medium. hard for those that are not comfortable rock hopping. 

Meeting: 7:00 am. Meeting place will be emailed closer to the time. Start and end location are on private property. Those accepted for the will be advised the location via email.

Distance: Approximately 7 kms round trip 

Walk Description:
Killymoon Creek, in the dry season, is a fantastic spot for rock-hopping enthusiasts. This walk start on a fire trail on private property with a few good hills to get everyone warmed up. The creek bed starts as a series of small rocky gullies which soon open up into a spectacular gorge.
We will have lunch at the swimming hole, where the polar bears amongst us can have a dip before lunch. This will be our turn around point and we will descend back down the creek from here.
This adventure will see us tackling numerous kinds of climbing. You will need to have a suitable level of fitness and coordination.

Duration:
Full day walk. Estimate back at the car park around 4 pm.

What to bring:
Advised equipment: Water (at least 4L as we cannot guarantee suitable water from the creek), Lunch (Snacks and electrolytes), Basic first aid, suitable sun safe clothing, sun screen, Mozzie spray and suitable shoes.

Speciality equipment: I strongly advise gloves as this walk requires a lots of hand work (but that’s just personal preference). You will need boots with plenty of tread for grip.
